C1814.title: Alias Robotics Unitree G1 Humanoid Robot Security Assessment
C1814.summary: In September 2025, Alias Robotics published a systematic security assessment of the Unitree G1 humanoid on arXiv. It found a command-injection vulnerability in the BLE provisioning flow, with all devices sharing one hardcoded AES key, allowing root within Bluetooth range. The FMX dual-layer proprietary encryption used a device-shared static Blowfish-ECB key (effective entropy 0). The robot sent battery, sensor, camera, and microphone telemetry to a China-based server (43.175.228.18:17883) every 300 seconds, violating GDPR. Researchers weaponized it as a covert surveillance node and attack pivot.
